page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-48xl is an x86_64 bare-metal instance deployed on dedicated Intel hardware. The platform provides 96 physical CPU cores and 192 vCPUs via multithreading, running at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. Because this instance operates directly on physical hardware without a hypervisor layer, workloads execute without virtualization latency or shared host resource contention.

The instance is provisioned with 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a general-purpose memory allocation ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is bundled directly into the chassis with 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency solid-state storage. For inter-node and external communication, the host features a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present on this model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server combines high core density, extensive on-board NVMe storage, and very high network throughput within a single bare-metal host. This integrated hardware setup reduces the need for external network storage attachments for IOPS-intensive workflows, though organizations must manage drive fault tolerance directly on the host. Hardware specifications align with high-capacity databases, low-latency key-value stores, distributed analytics, ETL processing pipelines, and large container virtualization environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server configured with 96 physical Intel cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 768 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4 GB RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally bundled via 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. It contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. By eliminating hypervisor overhead, this bare-metal platform offers direct access to physical compute, substantial local I/O capacity, and high-speed network interfaces. The consolidation of high compute density, extensive NVMe storage, and high networking throughput makes this instance appropriate for relational and distributed databases, real-time analytics, data warehousing, high-traffic web tiers, and containerized enterprise workloads demanding predictable physical hardware access.
